What the cylinder calculator does

A right circular cylinder has two equal, parallel circular bases joined by a curved side that meets them at right angles — the shape of a can, pipe or tank. Enter the radius (or diameter) and the height to get the volume, the curved (lateral) area, the area of the bases and the total surface area, with exact multiples of π wherever possible.

Try changing the input

Doubling the height doubles both the volume and the curved area. Doubling the radius multiplies the volume by 4 because the radius is squared.

Formulas and variables

LSA=2πrhTSA=2πr2+2πrh=2πr(r+h)V=πr2h
SymbolMeaning
rRadius of each circular base (half the diameter).
hHeight: perpendicular distance between the bases.
LSALateral (curved) surface area.
TSATotal surface area: curved side plus both bases.
VVolume: base area πr2 times height.

Why 2πrh? Cut the curved side along a vertical line and flatten it: you get a rectangle whose width is the circumference 2πr and whose height is h.

Worked example

A tank with radius 4 cm and height 10 cm

Step 1 — Known values

r=4 cm, h=10 cm.

Step 2 — Curved area

LSA=2π(4)(10)=80π≈251.33 cm2

Step 3 — Total surface area

TSA=2π(4)2+80π=32π+80π=112π≈351.86 cm2

Step 4 — Volume

V=π(4)2(10)=160π≈502.65 cm3≈0.503 L

Assumptions, domain and rounding

  • The cylinder is a right circular cylinder. An oblique cylinder has the same volume πr2h (with h measured perpendicularly) but a different lateral area.
  • Radius and height must be positive numbers.
  • An open container (such as a cup) uses LSA+πr2 rather than the total surface area.
  • Exact answers are shown as multiples of π; decimals are rounded to 6 places.
